title: U.S. Allies Have Midterm Fever
gist: Rachel Oswald reports that Canadians and Europeans are intensely tracking the 2026 U.S. midterms, with Canadians searching more than Americans per Google Trends, but experts warn a Democratic Congress cannot do much affirmatively to constrain Trump's foreign policy. The likeliest concrete outcome is an impeachment vote on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the week after the midterms and possibly a new inquiry in January.

insights.claim: Google search trends show Canadians, hit by some of Trump's harshest trade actions, searching for U.S. midterm information at a higher rate than Americans themselves.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Canada's intense focus reflects how much its trade outlook depends on U.S. political shifts.
insights.locator: Canadians, who have been on the receiving end

insights.claim: After Canada and the United States, midterm searches were highest in Denmark, Qatar and Norway, countries rocked by Trump's Greenland claims and the war against Iran.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Allied anxiety concentrates where U.S. policy has been most disruptive, flagging Greenland and Gulf exposure.
insights.quote: After Canada and the United States, midterm election information searches were the highest in Denmark, Qatar, and Norway
insights.locator: Europeans are also gripped by midterm fever

insights.claim: Center for American Progress official Damian Murphy says European officials are 'laser-focused' on the midterms, with granular knowledge of individual House races.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: European policymakers may be timing their positioning toward Washington around the midterm result.
insights.locator: Damian Murphy, the senior vice president

insights.claim: Damian Murphy cautions that Congress can do little affirmatively on foreign policy because the U.S. executive holds most of that power, but argues a Democratic win would send a global message that Americans repudiate ICE, the Iran war and the treatment of allies.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Investors should not expect a midterm result to reverse U.S. tariffs or foreign policy; the effect is signaling for 2028.
insights.quote: “What I’ve been telling them is that you shouldn’t have super high expectations for what any Congress can affirmatively do,”

insights.claim: Former French Ambassador Gérard Araud warns against overestimating a midterm defeat for Trump, noting presidential foreign-policy powers and that Trump can rely on the Supreme Court to bypass Congress.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Policy continuity through 2028 is the base case regardless of midterm outcome.
insights.quote: “Let us not overestimate the consequences of a defeat for the Trump administration in the midterm elections,”

insights.claim: Trump's surprise 2016 and 2024 wins keep foreign diplomats from expecting a blue wave, with one European diplomat saying the mission is to stamp out hope of a return to normalcy after the midterms.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Allied governments are planning for durable U.S. unpredictability rather than a reversion.
insights.quote: My mission is to stamp out any glimmer of hope of a return to normalcy after the midterms,”

insights.claim: A House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over alleged war powers and war crimes violations is likely the week after the November 2026 midterms.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Leadership turmoil at the Pentagon could affect the conduct of the Iran war and defense policy continuity.
insights.quote: A vote on the defense chief’s impeachment is likely to happen the week after the midterms.
insights.locator: One outcome with a strong chance

insights.claim: Even if Republicans protect Hegseth in the first vote, a new impeachment inquiry may be launched in January 2027 if Democrats win the House, as predicted.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Sustained congressional oversight of the Pentagon is likely in 2027 if the House flips.
insights.locator: Even if Republicans find the votes

insights.claim: Retired Canadian Maj. Gen. Scott Clancy says Hegseth deeply offended many Canadians by appearing to disparage Canadian cadets and denigrating NATO allied troops who served in Afghanistan.
insights.speaker: Rachel Oswald
insights.so_what: Personal frictions add to the erosion of U.S.-Canada and alliance goodwill.
insights.locator: The former Fox News host “deeply offended”
